title: Late Charge Scale Where a Level Plan on a Refined Fuels Account Has Fallen Away
content:
Where an energy balance under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts has run beyond the programme's grace period, the late charge raised on it answers how faithfully the level plan's standing monthly draft has been taken over the year.

**Where the days overdue stand beyond the programme's grace period and the plan's drafts were taken in fewer than 6 months over the twelve months ending on the handling date**, the late charge is 45.00 USD.

**Where the days overdue stand beyond the programme's grace period and the plan's drafts were taken in at least 6 months and in fewer than 11 months over that window**, the late charge is 30.00 USD.

**In every other case** the late charge is the programme's late charge where the days overdue stand beyond the programme's grace period, and nothing where they do not.

## The scale as a table

| Days overdue against the programme's grace period | Months in which a plan draft was taken, over the twelve months ending on the handling date | Late charge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Beyond the grace period | Fewer than 6 | 45.00 USD |
| Beyond the grace period | At least 6 and fewer than 11 | 30.00 USD |
| Beyond the grace period | 11 or more | The programme's late charge |
| Not beyond the grace period | Any number | Nothing |

The count is of the months in which a draft was taken, not of the money the drafts took. The days overdue must stand strictly beyond the grace period for any late charge at all: a balance standing exactly at the grace period is not beyond it.

*Hypothetical.* On a programme whose grace period is 10 calendar days and whose late charge is 15.00 USD, a member 25 days overdue whose drafts were taken in 4 months of the window is charged 45.00 USD. The same member with drafts taken in 8 months is charged 30.00 USD, and with drafts taken in 11 months is charged the programme's 15.00 USD. At 10 days overdue exactly, nothing is charged whichever the draft count.
